info.title: ATRIUM Translator API
info.description: Automated pipeline for the translation and enrichment of archaeological archival collections.

200.description: Alive; with `?deep=true`, the backends answer too.

422.description: Unusable or invalid input: request validation (`errors`), a bad parameter, a record that cannot be opened (`reason: invalid_record`), or a parameter or per-input budget over its limit (`reason: limit_exceeded`). Do not retry unchanged.

500.description: Processing failed. Report it; do not retry blindly.

503.description: `degraded`: the deep check failed, or the replica drains.

500.description: Processing failed. Report it; do not retry blindly.

200.description: The translated XML (`application/xml`, as an attachment). With a record sent, `multipart/mixed`: the XML, the record (`application/json`), `limits_applied.json` and `paradata.json` (the call's Process Run Crate `CreateAction`, `application/ld+json`). With `response_format=json`, one `TranslateResponse`.

X-Atrium-Limits-Applied.description: `key=effect:count; …` for each limit that applied; absent when none did.

422.description: Unusable or invalid input: request validation (`errors`), a bad parameter, a record that cannot be opened (`reason: invalid_record`), or a parameter or per-input budget over its limit (`reason: limit_exceeded`). Do not retry unchanged.

500.description: Processing failed. Report it; do not retry blindly.

413.description: The request content is over a limit (`reason: limit_exceeded`). Split the input or raise the limit.

415.description: Unsupported media type (`reason: unsupported_media_type`, with `accepted`). Do not retry unchanged.

503.description: Not ready, warming up or draining. Retry three times with backoff.

500.description: Processing failed. Report it; do not retry blindly.

AtriumDocument.title: ATRIUM document record
AtriumDocument.description: Per-document record built by accretion across the ATRIUM pipeline, schema 2.0 (doc-schema-v2, atrium-project#84). It holds content only: the identity of the original, its text in a form the enrichment steps work on, and what they add. No run data and no licence (D1, D2): which run wrote which blocks and fields is named by that run's paradata `result` (RO-Crate 1.2 / Process Run Crate 0.5 CreateAction). No copy of the layout (D26): blocks, tables, reading-order roles and page verdicts stay in the document's stored `atr/docproc-json`, and each line names its docproc block. The positional blocks (pages, content, lines) have one writer, the record builder (ocr-postprocess, D20). Keys removed in 2.0 are refused by name; any other unknown key passes, so a newer 2.x minor's additions survive a tool that vendored an older 2.x schema (rule 6). Produced by atrium_document.py; a 1.x record is migrated on load (migrate_document).
AtriumDocument.$comment: A record carries evidence that something was written into it: the source (the seed's identity) or at least one content block. A stage that ran and wrote nothing is refused (the #54 floor, without stamps since 2.0).

schema_version.description: Record schema version, MAJOR 2. A newer MAJOR than the reading tool supports must be refused; an older one is migrated (atrium_document.migrate_document).

record_type.description: 'atrium-document' for the normal linear accretion; '-merged' when parallel partial records were folded.

doc_id.description: Stable document identifier, carried unchanged by every tool. In the AMČR pilot it is the AMČR file id, written by the seed before the first stage (atrium-project#71); a tool keeps the baseline's value and never re-derives it from a file name.

source.description: The ORIGINAL input, named by the archive's SHA-512 (contract §5, H1). Intake (the AMČR seed, whose profile requires sha512, filename and media_type) writes the identity fields, first-writer-wins; the record builder adds language, page_count and origin. No path, no other digest. Absent on a standalone run that had no seed (rule 3).

sha512.description: SHA-512 of the original's bytes as the archive computed it (AMČR: the Fedora digest), lower-case hex. Written by the seed and carried unchanged by every tool (atrium-project#71).

language.description: Languages of the text, ISO 639-1 codes, dominant first.

origin.description: How the text was obtained, descriptive only (#84 §1): `digital` the text layer of a born-digital file, `atr` the ATR step, `legacy` converted PCSS (ABBYY) ALTO. It selects no writer: the positional blocks have one.

sha256.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — the original is named by its sha512 only (§6).

page_categories.description: Owner: page-classification. Predicted category per page label, for the pages that needed ATR (H3). Values come from the `page-category` scheme in the hub-canonical atrium_vocab.py -- 11 concepts, `atrium_vocab.labels_for('page-category')` -- and each has a stable URI via `atrium_vocab.concept_uri('page-category', value)`. Deliberately NOT constrained by `enum`: page-classification derives its label list from the filesystem at runtime (utils.py collect_images), so an enum here would turn a naming slip into a hard pipeline failure instead of the advisory NOTE the registry raises. See docs/skos_strategy.md 4.

pages.description: Owner of the rows: the record builder (ocr-postprocess), one row for every page of the original, empty pages included (D29). page-classification adds category fields to the pages that needed ATR; nlp-enrich adds teitok_surface. Field-level ownership — never co-mutated. The page's text-layer verdict and needs_atr live in docproc's routing (D27).

page.description: The printed page label as a string, so 'iv' or 'A-1' survive; written by the record builder, and what lines[].page and entities[].page name. Consumers must NOT derive ordering from it — use page_index.

page_index.description: The physical page number, 1-based: the row's key, the join key with docproc `pageNumber` (H2) and the ordering key. Every writer of a page row passes it.

content_status.description: `text`: the page has text; `empty`: it has none — no lines, no page score, counted apart in quality_summary (D29; D18 rule 7).

category.description: page-classification, on the pages that needed ATR (H3).

teitok_surface.description: Logical TEITOK <surface> id — an identifier, never an image path.

text_layer.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — the page verdict lives in the stored docproc's routing (D27).

needs_ocr.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — became `needs_atr` in docproc's routing (D27).

needs_ocr_reason.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — its reason is docproc's, with needs_atr (D27).

ocr.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — the engine is the producer's paradata (D9).

allOf.$comment: An empty page carries no page score (D18 rule 7).

content.description: Owner: the record builder. The text of the document, rebuilt in docproc's reading order, so the record never holds partial text (H8).

reading_order.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — reading order is docproc's (D26).

lines.description: Owner of the rows: the record builder (ocr-postprocess): text, box, docproc block, text source and box precision, and — as the line-quality model's owner (D18) — categ, quality_score and lang for every line. nlp-enrich adds lemma, upos, feats and teitok_ref. Field-level ownership. NOTE for validators: only page+line are required, so a row stripped of its text by a field-ownership filter still validates here — the round-trip assertion belongs in the writing tool.

page.description: Page LABEL, matching a pages[].page. A string for the same reason as there — 'iv' and 'A-1' must survive — so a writer must not pass an integer here: merge_block() keys rows on it, and a consumer sorting on int(page) needs pages[].page_index to order non-numeric labels.

line.description: 1-based, in reading order within the page; with `page`, the row's key.

bbox.description: The line's box in the one coordinate space ($defs/bbox); how it was obtained is bbox_precision.

block.description: The id of the docproc block this line belongs to (D26), e.g. `p3-b7`; on a mixed document, the ATR block that contains a kept text-layer line (H6).

text_source.description: Where the line's text came from (D25): the born-digital text layer, the ATR, or converted PCSS ALTO.

bbox_precision.description: How the box was obtained (D16, D25): measured for the line by its producer, derived from its docproc block, or none.

categ.description: Line category, the five values of the `line-category` scheme only (D18 rule 2). Written by the record builder for every line, whatever its text source. digital-convert's decode verdict (Garbage, Inverted) is a flag on docproc lines, never a category here.

quality_score.description: From the text alone: one model, one set of constants, one band scheme for every source (D18 rule 3).

lemma.description: nlp-enrich: UD lemma of the line's dominant token/lead form.

group_id.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — layout grouping is docproc's (D26).

style.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — layout cues are docproc's (D26).

entities.description: Owner: nlp-enrich; keyword-extract writes pid. `translation_en` is RESERVED, not in the pilot (contract §5). Carries all three tagsets so no mapping is lost. `page` and `line` are the record's line key; `bbox` is in the one coordinate space.

type_onto.description: OntoNotes v5 — the default configured NameTag tagset.

translation_en.description: RESERVED, written by no tool. Declared for the translator, which runs before nlp-enrich creates entities[]; English is produced only for free-text metadata in the AMČR pilot (atrium-project#70).

pid.description: FAIR ontology cross-references — the ARIADNE/GoTriple hook. Null until resolved.

translations.description: RESERVED, not in the pilot (contract §5): the translator's metadata-en is a record-level job and writes nothing into this record.

enrichment.description: Owner: keyword-extract (llm-enrich before 2026-10-01). Superset of the LLM document schema, plus the explicit page citation.

locator.description: Short verbatim snippet copied from the document.

page.description: Page label from the nearest PAGE_BREAK / '## Page N' marker.

teater_category.description: Single most relevant TEATER/AMCR vocabulary category: the source label as the vocabulary spells it (e.g. `kostel`), not an ATRIUM theme.

teater_category_ids.description: The AMCR and TEATER records `teater_category` stands for, by id: its own and those of the same label the vocabulary build merged into it. Written by keyword-extract; the RO-Crate names them by their source URIs (`https://api.aiscr.cz/id/<id>`, `https://teater.aiscr.cz/id/<id>`).

id.description: The record's id in its source (`HES-…` for AMCR).

keywords.description: Owner: keyword-extract (atrium-project#73). The STATISTICAL keywords of the document and of each page: KeyBERT by default, YAKE or KER (`legacy`) when a run asks for them; one run writes one method's lists. The controlled-vocabulary keywords are `enrichment`'s and never appear here, and the two kinds are never merged into one list. A score means something different per method (KeyBERT: a cosine in [0, 1]; YAKE: normalised per document to [0, 1]; KER: an occurrence count), so compare scores only within one list; `rank` orders every list from 1.

pages.description: The same per page, in page order; empty when the run asked for document keywords only.

quality_summary.description: Owner: the record builder, ocr-postprocess (atrium-project#73). A deterministic read-out of the stored quality fields, recomputed by atrium_document.quality_summary() whenever ocr-postprocess writes or scores pages and lines: statistics of `pages[].quality_score` and line counts per `lines[].categ`. Numbers only: no band, no threshold, and no tool reads it to route or refuse a document. `pages[].quality_score` stays the authoritative signal; a consumer that needs bands computes them from these numbers with its own thresholds.

pages.description: `total`: rows in pages[]; `empty`: those with content_status empty; `scored`: those with a quality_score; mean, median, min and max of those scores, absent when none is scored.

empty.description: Pages with content_status empty, counted apart (D18 rule 7).

lines.description: `total`: rows in lines[]; `by_categ`: rows per `categ` value (the `line-category` scheme). Rows without a category are `total` minus the sum.

provenance.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — run data and the calculated licence leave the record (D1, D2); the run's paradata describe it.

assembled.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — no stamps (D1): the run's paradata `result` names the blocks and fields it wrote.

derived_from.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — inputs are named in the run's paradata `object`, by distribution name and SHA-512 (D1, D23).

regenerable.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — a regeneration recipe is run data (D1).

tables.description: REMOVED in 2.0 — a table is docproc's `cellGrid`; its text stays in the record as lines (D26).

file.title: File
file.description: The XML to translate, its name ending in `.xml`: an ALTO page, or a metadata record such as AMČR's. Its root element decides which, unless `is_alto` is sent.

document_json.title: Document Json
document_json.description: Optional ATRIUM document record, or an AMČR seed (`doc_id`, `source`): its `doc_id` names the outputs. Since record schema 2.0 (atrium-project#84) the translator writes nothing into it: it comes back unchanged, as the second part of the multipart/mixed response, or as `document_json` with `response_format=json`. One that cannot be opened is refused (422 `invalid_record`). An empty part counts as none.

xpaths.title: Xpaths
xpaths.description: For a metadata record, required: the fields to translate, one XPath per line (AMČR's list, aiscr-webamcr#3570). The service has no default list; a metadata record without one is refused (422). Ignored for ALTO.

source_lang.title: Source Lang
source_lang.description: The source language, or `auto` (the default) to detect it. Also read from the query.

target_lang.title: Target Lang
target_lang.description: The target language; `en` by default. Also read from the query.

is_alto.title: Is Alto
is_alto.description: `true`: ALTO XML; `false`: AMČR metadata XML. Unset (since v1.6.0-beta): the upload's root element decides, `alto` or any other. Until then unset meant `true`, so a metadata record sent without it came back untranslated. Also read from the query.

fast_align.title: Fast Align
fast_align.description: ALTO only: distribute a block's translation over its lines by word counts instead of translating each line as an anchor (the command line's --fast-align): far fewer calls, coarser line splits. Default false. Also read from the query.

xsd_strict.title: Xsd Strict
xsd_strict.description: With `XSD_PATH` set, for a metadata record: `true` refuses a translation that does not validate (422), `false` returns it with `xsd_valid: false`. Default: the `XSD_STRICT` setting. Also read from the query.

include_log.title: Include Log
include_log.description: `true`: also return the translation log, the command line's `<doc>_log.csv` (`log_csv` with `response_format=json`, else a part of the multipart/mixed answer). Default false. Also read from the query.

include_record.title: Include Record
include_record.description: Kept for compatibility. Since record schema 2.0 the translator writes no record, so a record comes back only when `document_json` was sent. Also read from the query.

output_mode.title: Output Mode
output_mode.description: `replace` (the default, or the OUTPUT_MODE setting) or `append` — see issue #46. Also read from the query.

response_format.title: Response Format
response_format.description: `xml` (the default): the translated XML, or multipart/mixed when a record was sent or `include_record` or `include_log` is true. `json`: one `TranslateResponse` object with the XML as text, the record as `document_json` and the log as `log_csv`. Also read from the query.

@context.title: @Context
@context.description: The JSON-LD context: RO-Crate 1.2, plus the terms ATRIUM adds.

name.title: Name
name.description: A human-readable name of the run.

instrument.title: Instrument
instrument.description: The tool: a `SoftwareApplication` with `version`, its release page as `@id`, its repository as `url` and its authors as `creator`.

containerImage.title: Containerimage
containerImage.description: The image the service ran as (`ATRIUM_RUNNER_IMAGE`): `registry`, `name`, `tag`.

object.title: Object
object.description: The inputs, each by AMČR distribution name (`name`) and SHA-512 (`sha512`): the uploaded file and the record version sent with it. An input that is not stored carries `stored: false` (D23).

result.title: Result
result.description: The outputs, by distribution name and SHA-512. The record's (`atrium/document-json`) names the blocks and fields the call wrote in `recordFields`; an output that is not stored carries `stored: false`.

agent.title: Agent
agent.description: The organisation operating the service (`ATRIUM_RUN_AGENT`); absent when it is not set.

paradataRecord.title: Paradatarecord
paradataRecord.description: The run's atrium_paradata record (schema 3.0: no calculated licence), as the tool wrote it.

CreateAction.title: CreateAction
CreateAction.description:
The RO-Crate `CreateAction` of this call: its provenance (atrium-project#71 R2).

One Process Run Crate 0.5 action per call, as nested JSON-LD, built by
`atrium_rocrate.create_action()`; the same document an archive stores as the run's paradata
file. It names the tool as its `instrument` (with `version`, its release page as `@id` and its
authors as `creator`), the image as `containerImage`, the inputs as `object`, what the call
wrote as `result`, the `agent`, `startTime`/`endTime` and `actionStatus`, and the run's whole
paradata record as `paradataRecord`. Every service returns it with a successful response; its
`@id` is the run's `run_uuid`. Since doc-schema-v2 (atrium-project#84) the record carries no
stamps: the `result` names the record blocks AND fields the call wrote, and every input and output
is named by its AMČR distribution name and SHA-512.

status.title: Status
status.description: The HTTP status, as an integer.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: A registered reason code, listed with its statuses in the spec's `x-atrium-reason-codes`, or null when no code is registered for the cause. An open string: a release may add a code, but never renames or removes one.

limit.description: Only with `limit_exceeded`: the limit and the input's size.

errors.title: Errors
errors.description: The request-validation problems, or a structured detail.

accepted.title: Accepted
accepted.description: Only with `unsupported_media_type`: the file extensions or media types the endpoint reads.

cause.title: Cause
cause.description: A finer, unregistered cause (for example a reader's code). Informational; it may change.

ErrorBody.title: ErrorBody
ErrorBody.description: The body of every error a service returns (§4.4).

status.title: Status
status.description: `ok`, or `degraded` (HTTP 503) when the deep check fails or the replica drains.

in_flight.title: In Flight
in_flight.description: Deep check only: requests being served.

draining.title: Draining
draining.description: Deep check only: the replica is shutting down.

HealthBody.title: HealthBody
HealthBody.description: `GET /health`: liveness, and with `?deep=true` a check of the backends.

env.title: Env
env.description: The environment variable that sets it; null for a derived limit.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the current value came from: `env`, `config`, `default` or `derived`.

default.title: Default
default.description: The built-in default (not for a derived limit).

derived_from.title: Derived From
derived_from.description: For a derived limit: the settings it is computed from.

zero_means_unlimited.title: Zero Means Unlimited
zero_means_unlimited.description: True when 0 switches the limit off.

value.title: Value
value.description: The limit's value when it applied.

effect.title: Effect
effect.description: What it did: `sampled` or `split`. (`trimmed`, `skipped` and `stopped` fail the request since doc-schema-v2, D13; they appear only in notes written before it.)

LimitNote.title: LimitNote
LimitNote.description:
One limit that shaped a result without refusing it (the paradata `limits`, §4.5).

Since doc-schema-v2 (D13) only sampling and splitting are recorded: a limit that trims, skips
or stops content fails the request instead.

env.title: Env
env.description: The environment variable that sets it; null for a derived limit.

observed.title: Observed
observed.description: What the input measured; null when it is not known exactly.

effect.title: Effect
effect.description: Only when a limit trimmed, skipped or stopped content during processing (D13): that effect. The step failed; `observed` is the number of units affected.

LimitRef.title: LimitRef
LimitRef.description: Which limit a `limit_exceeded` refusal is about, and by how much.

type.title: Type
type.description: What the upload was translated as: `alto` (ALTO XML) or `metadata` (AMČR XML).

content.title: Content
content.description: The translated XML document, as UTF-8 text.

limits_applied.title: Limits Applied
limits_applied.description: Every limit that shaped the translation without refusing it (also the response header).

document_json.description: When a record was sent as `document_json`: that record, unchanged. The translator writes nothing into the record (record schema 2.0, atrium-project#84).

document_json_schema_error.title: Document Json Schema Error
document_json_schema_error.description: Only when the returned record does not validate: the schema error (the sent record's).

log_filename.title: Log Filename
log_filename.description: With `include_log=true`: the log's file name, as the command line writes it.

log_csv.title: Log Csv
log_csv.description: With `include_log=true`: the translation log (`file, page_num, line_num, text_<src>, text_<tgt>, status`), the `<doc>_log.csv` of the command line, as CSV text.

xsd_valid.title: Xsd Valid
xsd_valid.description: Only for a metadata record when the deployment sets `XSD_PATH`: whether the translation validates.

xsd_errors.title: Xsd Errors
xsd_errors.description: When `xsd_valid` is false: the validator's messages.

paradata.description: The call's paradata: its Process Run Crate `CreateAction` (paradata 3.0, atrium-project#84). For a metadata record, `object` is `metadata` and `result` is `metadata-en`, each by SHA-512; the field list and the language pair are parameters.

TranslateResponse.title: TranslateResponse
TranslateResponse.description: `/translate` with `response_format=json`: the translated XML and the record in one object.

service.title: Service
service.description: The tool id, which is the repository name.

version.title: Version
version.description: The tool version (`para_config.txt`), as in the release tag without the `v`.

limits.title: Limits
limits.description: Every limit of the service: `{key: effective value}`.

limits_meta.title: Limits Meta
limits_meta.description: For each limit: the variable that sets it, its unit, default, source.

openapi_sha256.title: Openapi Sha256
openapi_sha256.description: sha256 of this process's OpenAPI document in canonical form, equal to the `openapi.json.sha256` asset of the release the image was built from.

vocabulary.description: The vocabulary `/translate` applies, or null when `VOCABULARY_PATH` is unset.

xsd.description: The schema metadata translations are validated against, or null when `XSD_PATH` is unset.

file.title: File
file.description: The CSV's file name (not its path on the host).

with_description.title: With Description
with_description.description: Terms that carry a concept description.

sha256.title: Sha256
sha256.description: sha256 of the CSV, to tell two vocabularies apart.

file.title: File
file.description: The schema's file name (not its path on the host).

strict_default.title: Strict Default
strict_default.description: `XSD_STRICT`: whether an invalid translation is refused by default.

XsdInfo.title: XsdInfo
XsdInfo.description: The XML Schema metadata translations are validated against (`XSD_PATH`).

AtriumDocument_bbox.description: [x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max] in the ONE coordinate space of the record and docproc (D28): the displayed page, origin at the top-left of the CropBox, after /Rotate, y increasing downwards, in units of 1/72 inch × UserUnit (the page's canvas). Pages converted from PCSS ALTO whose original cannot be matched may be in px (canvas.unit).

AtriumDocument_canvas.description: The displayed page's size and the unit of every box on it (D28).

unit.description: `pt`: 1/72 inch × user_unit; `px`: only for PCSS pages whose original cannot be matched.

user_unit.description: The PDF page's UserUnit factor (name proposed in #84's implementation).

pixel_ratio.description: For an image docproc wraps into a PDF: image pixels per unit, the ratio back to the image (name proposed in #84's implementation).

AtriumDocument_entity_ref.description: A reference to one entities[] row by its natural key — BLOCK_KEY_FIELDS['entities'].

AtriumDocument_line_ref.description: A reference to one lines[] row by its natural key — the same key BLOCK_KEY_FIELDS['lines'] merges on. Survives merge_document_records(), which an array index does not.

AtriumDocument_statistical_keyword.description: One statistical keyword (`keywords`): the phrase, the method that found it, the method's own score (higher is more relevant) and its place in its list.

limit_exceeded.description: The input is over one of the service's limits. The body's `limit` member names it (`key`, the environment variable `env` that sets it, `value`, `observed`, `unit`). HTTP 413 when the request content is too large, 422 when a parameter or a per-input processing budget is exceeded, 504 when a time limit that depends on an upstream service expired. Split the input, or raise the limit.

busy.description: Every processing slot or queue place is taken (HTTP 429). Retry after the `Retry-After` header's number of seconds.

unsupported_media_type.description: The upload is not a type this endpoint reads (HTTP 415). `detail` says what was sent; the body's `accepted` member lists the file extensions or media types the endpoint accepts, and `cause` may name a finer, unregistered reason. Convert the input or send it to the tool that reads it; do not retry it unchanged.

invalid_record.description: The document record sent with the request cannot be opened (HTTP 422): it is not UTF-8 JSON, not a JSON object, or its `schema_version` has a newer major than this tool reads. Also sent when a block the tool adds rows to (`pages`, `lines`, `entities`) is not a list of objects. A record that opens but does not validate against the schema is otherwise accepted and reported in `document_json_schema_error`. Fix the record; do not retry it unchanged.

ocr_text_layer.description: DEPRECATED since doc-schema-v2 (atrium-project#84, H12): no service sends it. It meant: the PDF's text layer is an earlier OCR run's invisible text over page images (HTTP 422). Such pages are now marked `needs_atr` in docproc's routing, and the document goes through the ATR.

source_digest_mismatch.description: The record sent with the request names the original by its `source.sha512`, and the uploaded file is not that file (HTTP 422): the record would describe one file under another file's identity. Send the original the seed was made for, or a seed made for this file; do not retry unchanged.

upstream_unavailable.description: A backing service the tool calls (named at the start of `detail`, e.g. LINDAT UDPipe) did not answer after the tool's own retries (HTTP 502): it returned a server error, or refused or dropped the connection. The input is not at fault. Retry later with backoff. A backing service that timed out is a 504 `limit_exceeded` instead.
